title: Second derivative of a bounded Gaussian average
statement: Let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be measurable and satisfy $|f(z)|\le1$ for every $z\in\mathbb R$. For any positive variance $v$ and real $c$, the function $m\mapsto\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{z-m}{v}p_v(m,z)f(z)\,dz$ has derivative at $m=c$ equal to $\int_{\mathbb R}\left(\frac{(z-c)^2}{v^2}-\frac1v\right)p_v(c,z)f(z)\,dz$, where $p_v(m,z)$ is the Gaussian density with mean $m$ and variance $v$.
hypotheses_covered: $v$ is a nonzero nonnegative real, hence positive
replaced: Let $v>0$ and $p_v(c,z)=(2\pi v)^{-1/2}\exp(-(z-c)^2/(2v))$. If $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is measurable and $|f|\le1$, then for each real $c$ the derivative at $c$ of $m\mapsto\int((z-m)/v)p_v(m,z)f(z)\,dz$ is $\int((z-c)^2/v^2-1/v)p_v(c,z)f(z)\,dz$.
